content:
maria: FYI I landed the nightly krnlbench sweep results to the perf dashboard, and one candidate shows a consistent 12-18% 99p latency bump for short seqlen workloads on Ampere.
ashok: ugh, that sounds like the short-path kernel pick is doing the wrong fallback. Which candidate? commit/sha?
maria: candidate: krnl-cand-437b9 (autotune run 2026-03-17T23:10Z). Perf-CI shows it passing throughput tests but the microbench latency histogram spikes on seq_len=8 and 16.
perf-ci-bot: [alert] krnl-cand-437b9 nightly-scan: latency-regression detected (99p +15.2% vs baseline) on target: ampere-a10. Runs: 24/24. Logs: https://ci.internal/perf/krnl-cand-437b9
julia: do we have individual microprobe output? I want the kernel selection decision trace and KV cache hit distribution for those short inputs.
maria: pasted sample harness output below:
```
# harness run summary (seq=8)
selected_path: seq_short->fp16-packed-kv-v2
fallbacks: []
kv_cache_hits: 0.03
batch_size: 1
latencies_ms: p50=11.3 p90=21.7 p99=84.6
kernel_events:
  - init: kernel_load(fp16-packed)
  - dispatch: small_matmul_v2
  - exec: amx_fused_attention
```
noah: kv_cache_hits 0.03 seems wrong for short sequences — shouldn't prefix caching give higher hit rate even on first token scenarios for chat workloads?
linus: depends — the harness sample might be measuring cold-start only. Check longer-run steady-state where kv hits ramp.
maria: steady-state (seq=8, warm run after 50 requests): kv_cache_hits: 0.71, but lat p99 still ~78ms. Baseline kernel p99 ~66ms.
ashok: that suggests kernel itself has higher tail. Could be threading contention or a codegen regression on Ampere (shared scratch regs). Any perf counters (L2 miss / occupancy)?
julia: uploaded perf counters from perfprobe:
```
ampere-a10 - seq8 - p99 sample
L2_miss_rate=0.12
SM_occupancy=0.88
warp_serialize=0.03
avg_time_per_kernel_ms=1.9 (small_matmul_v2)
```
maria: compare to baseline run: L2_miss_rate=0.08 SM_occupancy=0.80 avg_time_per_kernel_ms=1.6
noah: L2 miss increase might explain tail. Candidate's kernel tile or prefetch policy might be less cache-friendly at short seq lengths.
perf-ci-bot: note: candidate also shows slight increase in aligned-memory ops vs baseline (+7%).
linus: can we repro locally with a focused microprobe that pins to Ampere and seqlen=8 with fixed kv state? I can run the microprobe and attach more traces.
ashok: please also run with `--disable-autotune` to force baseline kernel and `--force-candidate` to force new one. That will isolate whether selection logic or kernel code is at fault.
maria: running both now on perf-lab-ampere01. I'll post logs when done.

(10m later)
maria: results: with --disable-autotune (baseline): p99=65.9ms; with --force-candidate: p99=79.8ms. Kernel-level trace shows extra memclr step in candidate's init path on first dispatch.
julia: memclr? that smells like a zeroing optimization introduced in the candidate when allocating a temporary buffer. Could be unnecessary for small sequences.
noah: if that's the case, we should change candidate to lazy-zero or reuse buffers. Also need to update autotuner cost model to penalize the per-call startup cost for short seq.
linus: I ran microprobe with `--track-prefetch` and saw candidate issue prefetch distance too long for small L2 working sets; prefetches evict useful lines.
maria: proposed action items:
- linus: create a minimal repro microbench that demonstrates extra memclr/prefetch pattern and open PR to remove eager zeroing. (assigned)
- ashok: update autotune cost model to include p99 penalty for seq<=32 and add a warmup-sensitive term. (assigned)
- julia: add logging to kernel selector to record chosen kernel + prefetch/pref decisions into nightly harness artifacts. (assigned)
- perf team: re-run nightly sweep with patched candidate after PR merge and mark gating status to hold until p99 <= +5%.
ashok: SGTM. Also add a quick canary in perf CI to run seq8 short-tail microbench after merge.
maria: I'll annotate the perf ticket with these findings and link traces: https://perf.internal/tickets/PR-krnl-437b9-triage
julia: thanks everyone. @perf-ci-bot can you requeue the candidate job after we have the PR? :thumbsup!
perf-ci-bot: acknowledged. Requeue will be triggered once PR is merged and nightly hook updated.
maria: closing the loop here — will follow up when PRs exist. :wave:
